note: Iovino et al. BT survey: Halo 2 among first BT papers; FSM n^2 transition blowup vs BT function-call-like modularity; BTs in Nav2, ABB/KUKA/UR industrial robots; BT+planner hybrids for long-horizon tasks.
Nav2 official docs: behavior trees give navigation logic a formal structure that is verifiable and validated; reusable primitives and subtree composition; chosen over FSMs for scalability.
Attendee notes of Damian Isla's GDC 2008 Halo 3 AI talk: behavior trees run the individual AI under a declarative task/objectives layer; also records the talk's honest drawbacks.

Chris Hecker's shipped Spore behavior-tree docs (via Wayback Machine; live site returned a temporary-downtime page on 4 attempts): BT library as ticking HFSMs, Activate/Deactivate/Tick, prioritized deciders with hysteresis, static declaration, debug levels.
BehaviorTree.CPP repo (~4.3k stars, MIT, 2014-2026): C++17 BT engine with runtime-loaded XML trees, async actions, reactive/concurrent execution, logging to record and replay state transitions.
Groot2 IDE for BehaviorTree.CPP: drag-and-drop editing, real-time monitoring of a running executor, log replay at variable speeds, blackboard inspection and breakpoints in the PRO tier.

PORTAL (Agents Play Thousands of 3D Video Games): states 'the inherent latency of LLM inference renders them impractical for real-time applications'; generates BTs in a DSL executed at runtime, 'eliminating inference latency during gameplay' — a rival paper confirming the BT runtime architecture.
Unity Behavior package docs: official visual behavior-authoring tool for NPCs and gameplay logic with graph authoring and blackboard variables — BT authoring as engine-grade commodity.
LimboAI (~3.1k stars, MIT): Godot 4 C++ plugin combining behavior trees and hierarchical state machines, with editor, visual debugger, blackboard, and BT/HSM integration.

Ogren & Sprague, 'Behavior Trees in Robot Control Systems' (Annual Review of Control, Robotics, and Autonomous Systems 2022): modularity, hierarchies, and feedback as the control-theoretic foundations of BTs.
BT overview article: extensive use in high-profile games such as Halo, Bioshock, and Spore; task-not-state building block; robotics uptake (UAVs, manipulation, multi-robot).
Round 1: LLM-BT (Zhou et al. 2024) verified — ~85% cargo / ~75% household success, 5 cases x 20 users, with random external disturbances; in-place tree expansion on failure.
Round 1: LLM-as-BT-Planner (Ao et al.) verified — GPT-4 12/17 one-step and iterative, 16/17 only human-in-the-loop, recursive 13/17 at ~50k tokens; non-specific feedback gives no improvement.

Round 2: KRAFTON PUBG Ally (NVIDIA ACE) — 'A System 1 layer, implemented as a behavior tree, handles... movement, aiming, and immediate combat responses at game tick rate'; 'Reflex-level actions never have to wait for the model'; authored BT reflexes in a shipped co-op companion.

Round 3: SayCan (Ahn et al.) abstract verified — grounding comes from 'pretrained skills' and their 'value functions', i.e. learned competence, not authored response curves; used against the utility advocate's citation of SayCan as 'their exact shape'.
